messages:
Maya: Quick sync — we need to lock the Console observability scope for next release. Customers keep asking for: cost breakdowns, lightweight tracing hooks for tool-calls, and better error grouping. Can we triage must-haves vs nice-to-haves?
Sam: +1. My read: cost-per-route and per-model token split are high-impact for billing questions.
Liam: Agreed. Also want to make sure we don't blow latency on the hosted API when we add tracing. So 'lightweight' is key.
Anya: For error analytics, customers want user/session grouping and root-cause tags (e.g., model timeout, rate-limit, prompt error). That's reasonably scoped.
Jess: From PM side I'd prioritize: 1) cost breakdown (MVP: per-route + per-model daily) 2) error grouping (MVP: grouped by error class + sample trace) 3) tracing hooks (MVP: event snippets + span id) — others later.
Maya: Proposal: split into two milestones. Milestone A (launch criteria): cost breakdown + basic error grouping + dashboards for top-10 routes. Milestone B (post-launch): tracing hooks, deep trace linking, per-session analytics. Thoughts?
Liam: Works for infra. For tracing hooks we can expose a tiny SDK that emits span headers. But that will require runtime changes (kv-cache pass-through). Target Milestone B for that.
Sam: Can we define concrete launch criteria for Milestone A? Eg: cost per-route within 24h granularity, accuracy +/-5% on token attribution, dashboards with paging, and error grouping with sample rate 1% and ability to surface 5 sample traces per group.
Maya: I like that. Add SLA: dashboards must render under 2s for 95th percentile for <1000 routes.
Anya: For error grouping, we should support custom tags from customers (e.g., request_id, customer_tag). We'll accept as opt-in metadata in the payload. Add to scope?
Jess: Opt-in custom tags = Milestone A but beta only. Ship it behind a feature flag.
Liam: Action: I'll scope infra work. Need an experiment on trace sampling overhead.
Sam: Action: I'll own product requirements doc and the acceptance criteria. Will draft today.
Maya: Action: @Liam and @Anya pair on sampling test and prototype the grouping algorithm using last month's error logs.
Anya: Will run a quick clustering on the last 30 days and share top 10 clusters by volume.
ops-bot: deployment notice: Observability feature-flag toggles created on staging: ff/obs-cost-breakdown, ff/obs-error-grouping, ff/obs-tracing.
Jess: Rollout plan idea — soft launch to 3 pilot customers (two startups, one enterprise) for 2 weeks, collect telemetry and UX feedback, then widen.
Sam: Timeline ask: can we target internal launch (dogfood) in 3 weeks and public beta in 6 weeks?
Liam: 3 weeks for dogfood is tight but doable for Milestone A if we cut the dashboard to top-10 routes only and sample traces at 0.5%.
Maya: Okay set plan: dogfood in 3w (Milestone A limited rollout), public beta in 6w. Jess, coordinate pilot customers. Sam, send PRD by EOD.
Anya: One more perf note — cost attribution job will run as a daily batch at first. We'll surface near-real-time via an async cache but not guaranteed. Call out in docs.
Sam: Noted. Will add to PRD and call out accuracy/lag expectations.
Jess: UX ask — dashboard needs an export CSV button for cost slices and an inline 'investigate' button to open sample error traces.
Maya: Good. Keep exports simple for launch.
Liam: Dev tasks: infra metrics, job for cost attribution, feature-flag wiring, small DB schema for grouped errors, dashboard endpoints. I'll break down in tickets.
Maya: Dependencies: billing team for token attribution logic, infra for sampling hooks, docs for rollout runbook.
Sam: I'll enumerate dependencies in the PRD.
Maya: OK team — thanks. If no objections I'll freeze scope as discussed and create the roadmap card. Any last blockers?
Jess: None here. :+1:
Anya: All good.
Liam: No blockers.
Maya: Great — closing thread. I'll post the roadmap card and link pilots.
